findings.who: A couple filing jointly for 2025 who filed separate returns for 2024. Only the spouse itemized and deducted medical expenses, and the spouse's insurer reimbursed part of them in 2025.
findings.why_no: The parent condition reads 'you itemized deductions for 2024'. The filer did not itemize; the spouse did. So the Worksheet 2 helper is no, and the medical question is never asked.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 25: 'If you recover any itemized deduction that you claimed in an earlier year, you must generally include the full amount of the recovery in your income in the year you receive it.'
findings.fix: Ask 'Did you or your spouse itemize deductions on any 2024 return, joint or separate?' Use the itemizing spouse's 2024 Schedule A for the deduction and its limits.

findings.who: A filer whose health insurer or HSA/HRA reimbursed in 2025 medical bills that the filer had paid and deducted for 2024.
findings.why_no: 'Money was paid back for 2024' reads as a refund of something overpaid, such as a tax refund. An insurance reimbursement for a claim does not feel like money 'paid back'.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 26, Example 34: 'In 2025, you received a $500 reimbursement from your medical insurance for your 2024 expenses.'
findings.fix: Word the parent as 'In 2025, did you or your spouse receive any refund, reimbursement, insurance payment, or settlement for something you deducted on your 2024 Schedule A (taxes, medical bills, mortgage interest, and so on)?'

findings.who: A filer who paid a 2024 doctor or hospital bill. In 2025 the insurer paid the provider directly, and the provider refunded the filer's overpayment.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'reimbursement' as a payment from an insurer to them. The refund came from the provider, and the insurer paid the provider, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2: 'Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements.'
findings.fix: In the help, say that refunds from doctors, hospitals, pharmacies or insurers all count, whoever paid whom.

findings.who: A filer who deducted 2024 health or long-term-care insurance premiums as medical expenses and received a 2025 premium refund or rebate. Also a filer who received a 2025 lawsuit or accident settlement allocated to 2024 medical costs they deducted.
findings.why_no: A premium rebate or a damages settlement is not seen as a 'reimbursement of medical or dental expenses'. The filer thinks only of bills for care.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2: 'Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements.'
findings.fix: List examples in the medical question: insurance claim payments, refunds of insurance premiums you deducted, provider refunds, and the part of a settlement or damages award meant for medical costs.

findings.who: A filer reimbursed in 2025 for medical expenses deducted on a 2023 (or earlier) Schedule A, with or without 2024 recoveries.
findings.why_no: The gate and the questions ask only about 2024 itemizing and 2024 expenses. An earlier-year recovery gets a truthful no and is dropped.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 27, Worksheet 2: 'If you recovered amounts from more than 1 year, such as a state income tax refund from 2024 and a casualty loss reimbursement from 2023, complete a separate worksheet for each year.'
findings.fix: Ask whether any 2025 recovery relates to a deduction from a year before 2024. If so, run a separate Worksheet 2 per year, or refuse.

findings.who: A filer whose 2024 itemized deductions exceeded the standard deduction by more than all recoveries, with every one of the five statements true, as in Example 30, and who received a medical reimbursement.
findings.why_no: If 'Worksheet 2 is used' is computed false whenever full inclusion applies, the medical question is skipped. The $200 medical recovery is then lost unless another path collects it.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 25, Example 30: 'so you must include your total recoveries in your income for 2025 ... the balance of your recoveries, $525, on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8z.'
findings.fix: Gate on 'any 2025 recovery of a 2024 itemized deduction', not on whether Worksheet 2 is needed. Let the computation decide full or partial inclusion.

locators: p. 25, Example 30, "Medical expenses"
p. 26, Example 34, "In 2025, you received a $500 reimbursement from your medical insurance for your 2024 expenses"

p. 26, Example 34, "The only amount of the $500 reimbursement that must be included in your income for 2025 is $200, the amount actually deducted"; p. 26, Recovery limited to deduction, "The amount you include in your income is limited to the smaller of: • The amount deducted, or • The amount recovered"
p. 26, Recovery limited to deduction, "You don’t include in your income any amount of your recovery that is more than the amount you deducted in the earlier year"
p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2, "Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements"

findings.who: A couple who married in 2025 and file jointly for 2025. In 2024 the spouse filed single, itemized, deducted mortgage interest on their own home, and in 2025 the lender refunded part of that 2024 interest. The filer took the standard deduction in 2024.
findings.why_no: The parent helper says "you itemized deductions for 2024." The filer truthfully did not itemize, so the computed condition is false and the refund question is never asked.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 24: "If you received a refund or credit in 2025 of mortgage interest paid in an earlier year ... You may have to include it in your income"; p525 p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2: "Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements"
findings.fix: Ask whether you or your spouse received the recovery, and whether that person itemized on their own 2024 return (joint or separate). Run Worksheet 2 for each spouse's 2024 return where that applies.

findings.who: A filer with a seller-financed or private-lender mortgage who deducted 2024 interest on Schedule A line 8b with no Form 1098, and whose lender refunded overpaid 2024 interest in 2025. A co-op tenant-stockholder who received a refund of their share of the co-op's 2024 mortgage interest is in the same position.
findings.why_no: The question says "refunded (Form 1098 box 4)." With no Form 1098, or an empty box 4, the filer reads the form reference as the test and answers no.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 24: "the amount should be shown in box 4 of Form 1098" (should, not must); p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2: "all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements"
findings.fix: Ask: "In 2025, did any lender, co-op, or other payee refund or credit you any mortgage interest you deducted for 2024? It is often, but not always, shown in Form 1098 box 4."

findings.who: A filer whose lender found an overcharge of 2024 interest and, in 2025, credited it to the loan principal or escrow account instead of sending a check.
findings.why_no: The word "refunded" suggests money paid out. The filer received no payment and answers no.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 24: "If you received a refund or credit in 2025 of mortgage interest paid in an earlier year"
findings.fix: Say "refunded or credited (including a credit to your loan balance or escrow)."

findings.who: A filer who itemized for 2024 and whose only recovery in 2025 is a mortgage interest refund. There is no state tax refund.
findings.why_no: The parent helper says "money was paid back for 2024," which can be read as the filer repaying money. The six statements that trigger Worksheet 2 on p. 24 also name only taxes ("such as a general sales tax or real property tax refund"). So the filer, or the tool, concludes that Worksheet 2 is not used, and the mortgage question is never reached.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 24 statement 2: "You received a refund other than an income tax refund ... of an amount deducted or credit claimed in an earlier year"; Worksheet 2 line 2 covers "all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements"
findings.fix: Word the parent as "In 2025, did you or your spouse receive a refund, credit, or reimbursement of anything deducted on your 2024 Schedule A (taxes, mortgage interest, medical, casualty, etc.)?" Use Worksheet 2 whenever any non-income-tax recovery exists.

findings.who: A filer who received a refund in 2025 of mortgage interest paid partly in 2023 and partly in 2024, or entirely in 2023, and who itemized in those years.
findings.why_no: Both the parent and the child say "for 2024." The filer answers no, or reports only part of the refund, and nothing asks about the 2023 portion.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 24: "refund or credit in 2025 of mortgage interest paid in an earlier year"; "Recovery for 2 or more years ... you must allocate, on a pro rata basis"; p. 27: "If you recovered amounts from more than 1 year ... complete a separate worksheet for each year"
findings.fix: Ask which year's interest was refunded. Allocate the refund across years, and either support a separate Worksheet 2 for earlier years or refuse.

locators: p. 24, Mortgage interest refund, "You may have to include it in your income under the rules explained in the following discussions"
p. 24, Mortgage interest refund, "the amount should be shown in box 4 of Form 1098"; p. 27, Worksheet 2, footnote 2, "Don’t enter more than the amount deducted for the prior year"
p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2, "Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements"

findings.who: A filer who itemized in 2023 and took a casualty loss or medical deduction that year, then received the insurance reimbursement or refund in 2025. They took the standard deduction in 2024, or itemized in 2024 but nothing from 2024 was recovered.
findings.why_no: The parent gate and child question are fixed to 2024 ('paid back for 2024 and you itemized deductions for 2024', 'something else you itemized for 2024'), so a truthful no excludes recoveries of deductions from earlier years.
findings.irs_text: p525 (2025) p. 27, Worksheet 2: 'If you recovered amounts from more than 1 year, such as a state income tax refund from 2024 and a casualty loss reimbursement from 2023, complete a separate worksheet for each year. Use information from your tax return for the year the expense was deducted.'
findings.fix: Ask 'In 2025, did you or your spouse get back any amount (refund, reimbursement, rebate, credit or offset) of an expense deducted on Schedule A in ANY earlier year?' Then collect the deduction year and run one Worksheet 2 per year, using that year's Schedule A, standard deduction and taxable income.

findings.who: A married couple filing jointly for 2025 who filed separately in 2024, or were not yet married. The spouse itemized on a 2024 separate return and in 2025 received a refund of medical or mortgage interest from that year.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'you itemized deductions for 2024', so the filer answers about their own 2024 return and says no.
findings.irs_text: p525 (2025) p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2: 'Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements'; 'Use information from your tax return for the year the expense was deducted.'
findings.fix: Ask 'Did you or your spouse itemize on any prior-year return (joint or separate) and get back part of a deducted expense in 2025?' Run a worksheet for each prior return, using that return's figures.

findings.who: A filer who itemized 2024 medical expenses and in 2025 received an insurance reimbursement, or a damages award covering them. A filer whose 2024 casualty loss was reimbursed later.
findings.why_no: The words 'money was paid back' and 'a refund of something else' suggest a refund from the payee. An insurer's reimbursement, a later award or a rebate is not seen as 'paid back' or a 'refund'. The filer may also read 'money was paid back' as money the filer repaid.
findings.irs_text: p525 (2025) p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2: 'Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements (excluding the amounts you entered on lines 1a and 1b)'
findings.fix: Ask 'In 2025, did you or your spouse receive any refund, reimbursement, rebate, insurance payment, award or credit for an expense you itemized (medical, mortgage interest, casualty/theft loss, charitable gift returned, sales tax, other taxes)?' List the categories.

findings.who: A filer who deducted 2024 state and local general sales taxes instead of income taxes and got part of that sales tax back in 2025.
findings.why_no: The filer treats it as a 'state/local tax refund' already handled by the state tax refund questions (lines 1a/1b), not as 'something else you itemized'.
findings.irs_text: p525 (2025) p. 27, Worksheet 2, footnote 2: 'If you deducted state and local general sales taxes and received a refund of those taxes, include the amount on line 2'
findings.fix: Name the case in the child question or its help text: 'including refunds of state or local general sales taxes you deducted, refunded mortgage interest (Form 1098 box 4), and reimbursed medical or casualty expenses'.

findings.who: A filer whose lender reported 2024 mortgage interest refunded or credited in 2025 (Form 1098, box 4). Or a filer whose medical provider issued a credit to the account, or applied an overpayment to a later bill.
findings.why_no: No money was 'paid back' to them; the recovery came as a credit, offset or adjustment. So they answer the 'money was paid back' parent gate no.
findings.irs_text: p525 (2025) p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2: 'Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements'
findings.fix: Replace 'money was paid back' with 'you got back, were credited, or were reimbursed for any part of an amount you deducted', and mention credits and offsets in the help text.

locators: p. 27, Worksheet 2, footnote 2, "Don’t enter more than the amount deducted for the prior year"
p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2, "Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements (excluding the amounts you entered on lines 1a and 1b)"
p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2, "Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements"

findings.who: A couple files jointly for 2025. In 2024 the spouse filed a separate (married filing separately or single) return and itemized; the filer took the standard deduction. In 2025 the county refunded part of the real estate tax the spouse paid and deducted in 2024.
findings.why_no: The parent helper says 'you itemized deductions for 2024'. The filer truthfully did not itemize, so Worksheet 2 is treated as not used and the property-tax question is never reached. Only the gated question below mentions a spouse.
findings.irs_text: p525 (2025) p. 26, Worksheet 2a line 2: 'Enter the refunds received for state and local real estate taxes and state and local personal property taxes'
findings.fix: Word the parent gate as 'Did you or your spouse itemize deductions on a 2024 return, and did either of you get back in 2025 any amount deducted on it?' Ask the property-tax helper as 'you or your spouse' as well.

findings.who: A homeowner who itemized in 2024 won an assessment appeal in 2025. The county credited the overpayment against the 2025 tax bill, or sent it to the mortgage servicer, which applied it to escrow. No check came to the filer.
findings.why_no: 'money was paid back for 2024' and 'refund' read as cash received. A credit against next year's bill or an escrow adjustment does not feel like money paid back. 'Paid back' may also be read as money the filer repaid.
findings.irs_text: p525 (2025) p. 26, Worksheet 2a line 2: 'Enter the refunds received for state and local real estate taxes and state and local personal property taxes'
findings.fix: Ask 'In 2025, did you get back, or have credited to a later bill or escrow, any 2024 state or local tax, medical expense, or other amount you deducted on 2024 Schedule A?' Explain that credits, abatements and escrow pass-throughs count.

findings.who: A filer paid the 2023-assessment real estate tax bill in 2024 and deducted it on 2024 Schedule A. Part of that tax was refunded in 2025.
findings.why_no: 'a refund of 2024 real estate ... tax' reads as tax for assessment year 2024. The bill was labeled 2023, so the filer answers no. The line turns on tax deducted on the 2024 return, which means tax paid in 2024.
findings.irs_text: p525 (2025) p. 26, Worksheet 2a line 4: 'real estate taxes, and personal property taxes paid in 2024 (generally, this is the amount reported on your 2024 Schedule A (Form 1040), line 5d)'
findings.fix: Ask about 'real estate or personal property tax you paid in 2024 and deducted on your 2024 Schedule A, whatever tax year the bill was for'.

findings.who: A filer deducted the value-based part of a 2024 vehicle registration or excise fee, or received a state property-tax rebate or relief payment tied to 2024 tax paid on the home.
findings.why_no: The filer sees a registration-fee refund, an excise abatement, or a 'rebate' or 'relief check', not a 'refund of real estate or personal property tax'. Some of these programs pay out through the income tax system, so the filer files them under income tax refunds or answers no.
findings.irs_text: p525 (2025) p. 26, Worksheet 2a line 2: 'refunds received for state and local real estate taxes and state and local personal property taxes'
findings.fix: Add help text: 'Include refunds, rebates, abatements or credits of property tax on your home or land, and of the value-based part of vehicle registration, boat or excise taxes you deducted in 2024.'

findings.who: A filer who itemized in 2023 (not 2024) received a refund of 2023 real estate tax in 2025.
findings.why_no: The gate is framed only around 2024 deductions, so the filer correctly answers no. The taxable recovery of an earlier year's deduction then has no path in this flow.
findings.irs_text: p525 (2025) p. 26: 'The result of step 2 is the amount of the recovery to include in your income for the year you receive the recovery.'
findings.fix: State that recoveries of deductions from years before 2024 are handled elsewhere, and route them there.

locators: p. 26, Worksheet 2a, line 2, "Enter the refunds received for state and local real estate taxes and state and local personal property taxes"

findings.who: A joint 2025 filer and spouse who each filed separate 2024 returns and in 2025 received a state or local income tax refund for 2024 taxes deducted on those returns.
findings.why_no: The gate asks for an amount 'other than a state or local income tax refund,' so they answer no; the gated help says 'A state income tax refund counts as money back.'
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 1a: 'State/local income tax refund or credit'; and p. 27: 'If you recovered amounts from more than 1 year, such as a state income tax refund from 2024 ... complete a separate worksheet for each year.'
findings.fix: Remove the SALT exclusion from the gate or split it: ask the broad recovery question including state/local income tax refunds, then route SALT recoveries to the state refund worksheet; still ask the two-return question when separate 2024 returns are involved.

findings.who: A joint 2025 filer and spouse who each filed separate 2024 returns and in 2025 received an insurance reimbursement or other refund/reimbursement (not a literal 'payment back') for a 2024 casualty loss or other itemized deduction that lowered their 2024 tax.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether they were 'paid back'; they were reimbursed by an insurer or refunded by a seller, so they answer no even though Worksheet 2 covers refunds and reimbursements.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 27, Worksheet 2, line 2: 'Enter the total of all other Schedule A ... refunds or reimbursements'; line 1b covers state/local real estate and personal property taxes.
findings.fix: Use 'recovered, refunded, or reimbursed' instead of 'paid back' in the gate and the gated question.

findings.who: A joint 2025 filer and spouse who filed separate 2024 returns and in 2025 recovered an itemized deduction, but in 2024 they were subject to AMT or their credits reduced regular tax to zero, so they believe the deduction did not lower their tax.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether the deduction 'lowered your tax'; they answer no because their 2024 tax was already zero or AMT-limited, not knowing the IRS requires refiguring and may treat the recovery as reducing tax.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 27: 'If you were subject to the AMT or your tax credits reduced your tax to zero, see Unused tax credits and Subject to AMT under Itemized Deduction Recoveries'; 'A recovery is included in income only to the extent of the deduction amount that reduced your tax ...'
findings.fix: Ask broadly whether they recovered an amount they deducted or claimed a credit for, and determine the tax benefit in the worksheet; add help that AMT/credits require refiguring rather than an automatic no.

findings.who: A joint 2025 filer with 2025 recoveries from deductions on more than one earlier year—for example, a 2023 casualty-loss reimbursement and a 2024 non-SALT deduction recovery—but not two 2024 returns.
findings.why_no: The gated question asks only whether the money was for deductions on 'two 2024 returns'; they answer no because they have one 2024 return and one 2023 return, so the tool then asks about only one return.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 27, Worksheet 2: 'If you recovered amounts from more than 1 year, such as a state income tax refund from 2024 and a casualty loss reimbursement from 2023, complete a separate worksheet for each year. Use information from your tax return for the year the expense was deducted.'
findings.fix: Broaden the gated question to 'more than one year or more than one return' and require a separate worksheet/refusal for each year; do not limit it to two 2024 returns.

locators: p. 27, Worksheet 2, "Use information from your tax return for the year the expense was deducted"
p. 27, Worksheet 2, "complete a separate worksheet for each year. Use information from your tax return for the year the expense was deducted"

findings.who: A filer who itemized on Schedule A for 2023 but took the standard deduction for 2024; in 2025 they received a casualty-loss reimbursement for 2023.
findings.why_no: The printed gate says 'money was paid back for 2024 and you itemized deductions for 2024,' so after answering yes to an earlier-year recovery they answer no to the 2024 itemization helper; Worksheet 2 separately requires a worksheet for the 2023 recovery.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 27: 'If you recovered amounts from more than 1 year, such as a state income tax refund from 2024 and a casualty loss reimbursement from 2023, complete a separate worksheet for each year.' Line 2: 'Enter the total of all other Schedule A (Form 1040) refunds or reimbursements'.
findings.fix: Gate on any recovery of a Schedule A deduction in any earlier year; ask the recovery year and whether the filer or spouse itemized for that year, then route to a separate Worksheet 2 per year, not a 2024-only path.

findings.who: A joint 2025 filer whose spouse, not the filer, itemized on a separate 2024 return and in 2025 received a refund or credit of 2024 mortgage interest.
findings.why_no: The first helper asks 'you or, on a joint return, your spouse,' but the second helper asks only 'Did you itemize deductions on Schedule A for 2024?'; the filer truthfully says no for himself and the spouse's recovery is silently zeroed.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 24: 'If you received a refund or credit in 2025 of mortgage interest paid in an earlier year, the amount should be shown in box 4 of Form 1098.'
findings.fix: Second helper should read 'Did you or your spouse itemize deductions on Schedule A for 2024?' and the gated questions should likewise include the spouse.

findings.who: A filer whose 2025 Form 1098 box 4 reports a credit from the lender for 2024 mortgage interest, rather than a cash refund.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether they were 'paid back an amount'; a lender credit is not money paid back, so they answer no, although the IRS line expressly covers a refund or credit.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 24: 'If you received a refund or credit in 2025 of mortgage interest paid in an earlier year, the amount should be shown in box 4 of Form 1098.'
findings.fix: Use 'refund, credit, reimbursement, rebate, or other recovery' rather than 'paid back'.

findings.who: A filer who itemized in 2024 but whose itemized deductions exceeded the standard deduction by only $250; in 2025 they recovered $2,100 of those deductions.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether they were paid back an amount whose deduction 'lowered your tax.' Knowing that only $250 of the itemized deductions had tax benefit, they answer no for the $2,100 recovery; Worksheet 2 would include $250.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 25, Example 32: 'Include $250 of the recoveries in your 2025 income. This is the smaller of your recoveries ($2,100) or the amount by which your itemized deductions were more than the standard deduction ($29,450 - $29,200 = $250).'
findings.fix: Gate should ask only whether the filer received a recovery of an amount deducted on a prior Schedule A; let Worksheet 2 apply the tax-benefit, standard-deduction, AMT, credit, and negative-income limits.

findings.who: A filer whose 2024 taxable income was negative by $200 and whose itemized deductions exceeded the standard deduction by $250; in 2025 they recovered $2,100.
findings.why_no: They see that they had no 2024 taxable income and answer no because the deduction did not lower any tax; but IRS Example 33 includes $50 of that recovery.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 25, Example 33: 'You must include $50 in your 2025 income, rather than $250.'
findings.fix: Do not ask the filer to decide tax benefit at the gate; ask broadly for Schedule A recoveries and compute the negative-taxable-income limitation in Worksheet 2.

findings.who: A filer who paid $1,700 of 2024 medical expenses, deducted only $200 because of the AGI floor, and in 2025 received a $500 insurance reimbursement.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether they were paid back an amount whose deduction lowered tax; the $500 reimbursement exceeds the $200 deductible amount, so they answer no. The gated medical question also asks about expenses 'you deducted,' and they did not deduct the full $500. IRS Example 34 includes $200.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 26, Example 34: 'In 2025, you received a $500 reimbursement from your medical insurance for your 2024 expenses. The only amount of the $500 reimbursement that must be included in your income for 2025 is $200, the amount actually deducted.'
findings.fix: Ask whether any reimbursement was for medical expenses included in a prior Schedule A deduction, not whether the whole reimbursement was deductible; then limit to the amount actually deducted.

findings.who: A filer who deducted state and local general sales taxes on 2024 Schedule A and in 2025 received a refund of those sales taxes after returning a large purchase.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'other than a state or local income tax refund'; the filer reads the exception as excluding state or local tax refunds generally and answers no, even though a general sales tax refund is not an income tax refund and belongs on Worksheet 2 line 2.
findings.irs_text: p525 p. 27, Worksheet 2 footnote 2: 'If you deducted state and local general sales taxes and received a refund of those taxes, include the amount on line 2'.
findings.fix: Explicitly include general sales tax refunds and distinguish them from state or local income tax refunds in the gate and help text.

locators: p. 24, Deductions not itemized, "If you didn’t itemize deductions for the year for which you received the recovery of an expense that was deductible only if you itemized, don’t include any of the recovery amount in your income"; p. 24, Itemized Deduction Recoveries, statement 2, "You received a refund other than an income tax refund, such as a general sales tax or real property tax refund"
p. 24, Mortgage interest refund, "If you received a refund or credit in 2025 of mortgage interest paid in an earlier year, the amount should be shown in box 4 of Form 1098"
